description: We are a team of ambitious individuals passionate about AI, technology, and innovation. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to develop our skills, gain practical experience, and collaborate to solve real-world problems using NASA’s open data. Our long-term vision is to build an AI startup that creates innovative solutions. We welcome motivated teammates who want to learn, grow, and turn ideas into reality.
summary:
HEALTH_E is a browser-based educational prototype developed by Team METH for the Astronauts Health challenge. It brings together three experiences: a seven-stage interactive space-health narrative, a dashboard for manually entering selected health indicators, and a CSV analyzer that plots heart rate, SpO₂, body temperature, and cabin CO₂, with rule-based anomaly flags.
The project responds to the challenge by showing how mission-relevant health information could be presented in a visual interface for crew review. This matters because long-duration missions expose astronauts to health hazards, while distance from Earth can make clear communication especially important. HEALTH_E demonstrates a possible way to explore health topics and sample indicators together; it is not a validated medical tool. Its sample data and hard-coded rules should not be used to make care decisions.
details:
HEALTH_E is a browser-based educational prototype with three complementary modules. Its seven-stage narrative includes Explorer and Science modes and an interactive 3D scene to introduce spaceflight-health topics. The monitoring page lets users enter 11 selected indicators—such as heart rate, blood pressure, body-mass change, sleep and reaction time—and displays summary cards, charts and rule-triggered messages. Its built-in scenarios are synthetic examples. The analysis page accepts a user-selected CSV containing a time field and heart rate, SpO₂, body temperature and cabin CO₂; it plots the values and flags observations using programmed limits and a rolling statistical check. These pages do not share a medical record or connect to live sensors.

The prototype aims to make selected health topics and sample indicators easier to explore and review. Its creative approach is to pair an interactive educational narrative with separate, practical-looking monitoring and telemetry demonstrations. This may support awareness and discussion, but no usability study or health benefit has been measured.

The supplied project uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Three.js and GLTFLoader for 3D content and browser-side charts and CSV handling. No dedicated medical hardware or live sensor integration is documented. Design considerations included spaceflight hazards, clarity of information, and distinguishing synthetic examples and software flags from clinical findings. Thresholds and messages are not clinically validated, so they should not guide treatment or operational decisions.
